t: Introduction and overview — U-2 Dragon Lady
name: Introduction and overview — U-2 Dragon Lady — aircraft record
title: Introduction and overview — U-2 Dragon Lady
description: Introduction and overview of the U-2 Dragon Lady: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history. The U-2 Dragon Lady is a single-engine high-altitude reconnaissance aircraft built by Lockheed, entering service in 1956. Flying above 70,000 feet, it photographed denied territory through the Cold War and beyond; one was shot down over the Soviet Union in 1960. 104 were built; upgraded U-2S aircraft still fly today. Baseline facts: High-altitude reconnaissance aircraft; service from 1956; 104 built by Lockheed; still flying..
how_it_works: Wings generate lift from airflow; the engine provides thrust; control surfaces and fly-by-wire or mechanical controls steer the aircraft in three axes.
